reason: The named cache-conflict experiment is my role: padding transposed-A rows changes the 2048-byte spacing at n=512 by a bounded 3.125% scratch increase. The supplied evidence does not prove set conflicts, so test it early and treat timing as the only performance evidence. Next are compute scheduling and full-tile store-path changes, which avoid packing cost and have concrete compiler or primary-source motivation; store proposals overlap heavily and should be treated as alternatives. Then test changes with broader memory traffic or structural scope. The B-panel proposals substantially duplicate one another, and the combined two-panel proposal uses the full stated L1D capacity before other data; packing cost is unknown. Historical paired-load results are a clear regression, while current baseline scores vary widely, so no proposal earns a promotion claim from them. Rank is experiment priority, not a claim that any change will win.
